newsitem.title: POLAND: Gripen consortium may offer Poland jet assembly.
newsitem.headline: Gripen consortium may offer Poland jet assembly.

text.p: A consortium of British Aerospace and Saab, planning to bid in Poland's tender for fighter jets, said on Wednesday its offer could include assembly of jets and engines at Polish plants.

John Weston, Group Managing Director of British Aerospace, told a news conference the industrial cooperation package that would accompany the consortium's offer, could include assembly of its Gripen fighters at the PZL-Mielec plant and engines in WSK Rzeszow.

"The partnership could involve final assembly of Gripen aircraft for Poland in PZL-Mielec plant as well as of RM12 engines in Rzeszow and this production could be Poland's input in Gripen sales on international markets," Weston said.
Weston said the industrial package could also include civilian projects in such areas as carbon fibers production, civilian aircraft industry, energy and agriculture.
Poland, which is seeking to replace its outdated communist-era fighter jets with about 100 modern machines, has yet to announce a tender for the contract.

But major makers McDonnell Douglas Corp, Lockheed Martin Corp, British Aerospace and Saab and Dassault have already been promoting their aircraft and presenting cooperation offers for Polish industry.

The British Aerospace-Saab officials would not give a specific estimate of how much the industrial package could be worth but Alan Garwood, the British firm's Managing Director for Europe and North America, said its value should roughly match the value of other offers.
He said the group's offer would involve a transfer of technology and allow Polish firms become a part of consolidating European arms industry.
Asked whether the consortium would consider equity investments in Polish subcontractors Garwood said:
"The answer is 'yes' if the investment was sensible and look at our track record -- we have equity-based investments in Germany, Holland, France, United States etc."
